An article on a health application for supervising community care sites (SSC App on IASO, exporting to DHIS2); its 'registries' are of health sites and community health workers. It names no civil registration or identity system and states nothing about the registration of births or deaths.

A research response on documents issued by the Congolese National Police (reports, wanted notices, appearance notices); it names no civil registration or identity system and states nothing about the registration of births or deaths.

A regional brief whose passages name DR Congo only in lists: GovTech group C, World Bank digital and GovTech projects, an ID4D Diagnostic, and GEMS. No civil registration or identity system is named or described for DR Congo.

systems.owner: Commission électorale nationale indépendante (CENI)
systems.tiers: Registration Centres (Centres d'inscription) open during registration periods, where the card is printed on the spot; prior registration can be verified on a CENI computer server; serves in practice as the only identity card

note: A research response on the voter card, an electoral register and so out of scope. Its mentions of civil status are the birth certificate as one accepted proof of identity and the civil-status details printed on the card; it states nothing about civil registration offices.

systems.owner: Office National d'Identification de la Population (ONIP), which constitutes and maintains it; held only on national territory
systems.tiers: not stated: created in law by Decree 22/07 of 2 March 2022, with compulsory registration and a national identification number given at first registration; the decree does not say it is in operation

systems.system: automatic update of the FGP through civil status
systems.country_label: mise à jour automatique à travers l'état civil
systems.owner: ONIP; authorities holding the data must communicate them regularly to the FGP (Article 11)
systems.tiers: not stated: provided for in the decree (Article 6.2), which also has the FGP hold birth and death act numbers and the registration numbers of a person's civil-status acts (Article 9); no operating link described

systems.country_label: registres communaux et territoriaux de la population
systems.owner: not stated

systems.owner: not stated; governed by the Family Code
systems.tiers: not stated; named only as the registers the FGP is to be updated from and harmonised with

note: A decree creating the population file, an identity system. It names the civil-status registers only as a source for that file and states nothing about how a civil registration office records a birth or death. The captured text stops in Article 18.

A deal record for a UK grant to the World Bank's ID4D initiative across more than 30 governments; DR Congo appears only in a list of ID4D priority countries. No system is named for DR Congo and no sum is attributed to it.

slug: 2017-01-01 AU - Report on the Status of Civil Registration and Vital Statistics in Africa
note: Continental survey (October 2016 round) reporting counts of countries, not country answers; its only statement on DR Congo's digital registration is the annex placing it in the under-35-per-cent band of the composite digitization score, which names no system and maps to no aspect value.

systems.owner: Commission Electorale Nationale Indépendante (CENI)
systems.tiers: Centres d'inscription, supervised by antennes and provincial executive secretariats

note: Voter identification and enrolment law (coordinated text, captured as an excerpt to Art. 21): an electoral register, out of scope; civil registration appears only as the birth certificate accepted as proof of identity and age (Art. 10).

facts.fact: The Family Code as amended by Law 16/008 of 15 July 2016 has every birth, marriage and death entered as an act in a separate bound register whose blank leaves are numbered and initialled by the public prosecutor's officer, written out without gaps or abbreviations and closed by the civil-status officer at each year's end (Arts. 82-84); the captured articles provide for no electronic record.
facts.system: registres de l'état civil

systems.country_label: registre de naissance, de mariage, de décès; registre supplétoire
systems.owner: Officier de l'état civil: mayor, bourgmestre of the commune, chief of the secteur or chefferie, head of diplomatic or consular mission; or a State agent named by the provincial governor
systems.tiers: Bureau principal at the seat of each commune, secteur or chefferie; bureaux secondaires created by the provincial governor; a named officer may be posted to a groupement, a health zone or a reference hospital

note: The capture is an excerpt ending in Art. 84; the Code's later civil-status articles were not read because they are not in the file.

systems.owner: UNICEF DRC as grant recipient; funded by Global Affairs Canada

note: A deal record: Global Affairs Canada's CAD 8,000,000 grant to UNICEF DRC, 2015 to 2018, closed 2018-12-31, described as raising birth registration through unnamed technology-enabled systems with mobile-based data capture and digital certificate issuance; it states an aim, not what any office does or where the record is made, so the system cannot be classed.

About the 2020-2024 justice reform programme; its audiences foraines are mobile criminal-court hearings that relieved prisons and pre-trial detention, not late birth registration, and its four systems (SIGMA, SIGAJ, SIGE, SIGCJ) are justice-sector tools outside the study's field.

Passages of the 2023 Digital Code: civil status appears only in a definition listing the Registre National de la Population as identity register, civil-status register and biometric register, as an item of personal data (Art. 183) and in a penalty clause (Art. 314); nothing on how or where a birth or death is registered.
